$comment: The Explore canon. Every preset is also a worked example of the Build grammar, so each must be expressible as {dataset, measure, dimension, period, filters}. If a preset cannot be expressed in the builder vocabulary, either extend the vocabulary or drop the preset. A chart whose dataset has a definition in dimensions.json renders that definition.
evergreen_test: Would this chart still be worth showing in 2035? If the title names a specific scheme, brand or year, it fails and belongs in the events layer instead.

$status.$comment: Every preset carries a status, so the gap between the canon and what the cube can serve is visible rather than discovered chart by chart. The UI renders anything not live as a 'coming when X lands' entry, and cross-checks the authored status against what the cube actually resolves: a disagreement is shown as a warning, because a stale status is worse than none.
$status.live: Renders from the cube as built.
$status.blocked: Correctly specified. Waiting on a deliverable named in requires.
$status.invalid: The preset's own configuration is wrong. requires names the fix.
$status.precedence: status is the worst outstanding state; requires lists every outstanding item, not just the worst.
$status.on_unblocking: When a dataset a preset waits on lands, re-run the triage before building the chart. The canon was written well ahead of the data, so some blocked presets will want rewriting rather than unblocking.

$note_templates.$comment: A note that states a figure must be templated from the build, or it drifts the moment the data moves. note_template resolves {dotted.path} against the manifest, the preset's dataset entry in it, and the preset's measure and dimension definitions; |pct formats a proportion. A plain note may not contain a figure at all: the UI flags one that does.

$composite.$comment: A deliberate, closed exception to one-chart-one-question, for the two questions that only exist as a comparison of two series. Not a sixth shape: both render through the trend renderer. Composite presets are never offered in the builder, and the UI flags them as a curated comparison so a reader does not mistake them for something the grammar can express.

defaults.$comment: Chart-level defaults that are not per-preset decisions. mix_smoothing: monthly share on survivors data swings too hard to read, so a mix chart defaults to a trailing share and offers monthly as a toggle. top_n_basis: which window ranks the values that keep their own line; the rest become one remainder series.
defaults.$colour_slots_comment: The line palette has eight colours (src/lib/theme.ts: no set of colours keeps more lines apart under colour blindness). On a mix chart the first colour_slots_by_trailing go to the largest series over the trailing window, the rest by peak rolling share over the preset's period, and any series beyond the palette is drawn as a grey context line. 5 keeps every current contender on the owner_country chart in colour while leaving three slots for the categories that carried earlier decades.

mix_default_start.$comment: A mix chart over all time crushes its story into the right of the frame whenever the dimension spent decades with one category. The default start is the first month the dimension had something to show: at least min_categories categories above min_share, sustained for sustain_months, measured on the 12-month rolling mix so it does not move with monthly noise. All time stays available as a toggle and is never the default. Computed in the browser, like the rolling share and the suppression guards, so these numbers change without a rebuild.
mix_default_start.$threshold_note: min_share 0.005 puts powertrain at 2009-10, where hybrids first became visible; 0.02 puts it at 2018-07 and hides the nine-year ramp. Do not lower it below 0.004: at 0.003 powertrain falls back to 1938-01, because 1940s diesel sat near 0.36% and the now-extinct Other category near 0.71%. The qualifying run is 202 months and the nearest non-qualifying run is 5, so sustain_months is what rejects the mid-century near-misses.
mix_default_start.$cardinality_note: Only low-cardinality dimensions. The test measures diversity, and diversity saturates immediately when a dimension has hundreds of values: on make it returns whatever month the denominator floor allows and the composition clause never binds.

presets.question: Which countries own the brands we register?
presets.note: Ownership is as at today, not at registration. A Fuso registered while Daimler Truck controlled it counts as Japanese-owned, because ARCHION owns Fuso now. This chart answers who owns these brands now.

presets.question: How has each powertrain's share of registrations changed?
requires: segment_group promoted to a dimension in config/dimensions.json. It is a column in segment_map.csv, not a dimension, so the filter resolves against nothing. Promotion changes what the pipeline emits, so it waits for the 8 November gate.
a powertrain x segment_group pair slice, so the filter can be applied rather than described

presets.question: New or second-hand? The balance over time.
presets.note: These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, and new and used vehicles leave the register at different rates, so an older month's split may differ from what was bought at the time. In recent cohorts used imports leave faster, which understates their share; in some older cohorts it runs the other way.

presets.question: How old are used imports when they arrive?
requires: the used_imports dataset, which needs an import_status x age_at_registration_band pair slice
presets.note_template: Most arrive aged {manifest.used_import_age_trailing.cluster.0} to {manifest.used_import_age_trailing.cluster.1}: {manifest.used_import_age_trailing.share_cluster|pct} of arrivals over the trailing {manifest.used_import_age_trailing.window_months} months, with a median of {manifest.used_import_age_trailing.median}.

presets.question: Which brands or manufacturer groups are gaining and losing ground?

granularity_options.label: Brand
granularity_options.note: Share, not volume. These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, so older months are thinned by scrappage and a count would partly measure it. Share removes the shrinkage every brand shares, but brands leave the register at different rates, so older months lean towards brands whose vehicles stay registered longer. Volume charts wait for true monthly registrations.

granularity_options.label: Parent group
granularity_options.note: Share, not volume. These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, so older months are thinned by scrappage and a count would partly measure it. Share removes the shrinkage every group shares, but groups leave the register at different rates, so older months lean towards groups whose vehicles stay registered longer. Volume charts wait for true monthly registrations. Group ownership is as at today, not at registration. A rising remainder here is the market fragmenting across groups too small to rank; the concentration chart measures that directly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

Share removes the shrinkage every brand shares, but brands leave the register at different rates, so older months lean towards brands whose vehicles stay registered longer. Volume charts wait for true monthly registrations.

presets.question: Which vehicle models lead the market?
requires: the registrations_flow dataset (build step 1b), so models are ranked on registrations rather than survivors (D-024), and a model breakdown in it
presets.note_template: Ranked by vehicles first registered over the trailing {dataset.coverage_trailing.window_months} months. Rank movement compares against the 12 months before. Only the {dataset.model_cap.model.cap} models with the most registrations are named; the rest roll into other.

presets.question: Is the market getting more crowded?
presets.note_template: The combined share of the {measure.top_n} largest brands in each month. Membership is recomputed monthly, so the line reflects concentration rather than the fortunes of a fixed set of brands. A falling line means the largest brands hold less of the market: more brands may be competing, or the same brands may be sharing it more evenly. In the early decades, makes with no match in the brand list count in the total but never take a place, which holds the line down.

presets.question: Cars, utes, vans or trucks?
presets.note: The register records most SUVs as station wagons, so they count as cars here.

presets.question: Which vehicle years can't we import any more?
requires: the used_imports dataset, which needs an import_status x age_at_registration_band pair slice
presets.note_template: At the {manifest.latest_snapshot} snapshot the oldest vehicle year arriving in volume is {manifest.moving_cutoff_vehicle_year}, an age of {manifest.moving_cutoff_age}. The closed band is fixed in vehicle year, so the cutoff's age rises by one each year and the gap moves rightward through this chart. The rule that closed it is on the events layer.

presets.question: How long do vehicles stay on the road?
requires: the registrations_flow dataset from the Stats NZ TPT series (build step 1b)
two or more archived snapshots in data/snapshots/
a renderer for the cohort_survival derived measure
presets.note: Of the vehicles first registered in a given year, what share is still registered later. Every figure states its base and the first snapshot in which the cohort was observed.
